游戏内容看起来很多，但是说实话并不“好玩” 一是UI易读性和易用性比较差，很多反直觉的操作，比如鼠标移到羁绊上看不到效果，还需要右键一下、棋子详细属性点开之后会一直悬浮，需要手动关闭、一些常用的元素分布在屏幕四个角，需要到处分神去看，照搬爬塔的界面不是一个明智的选择。 二是没有意识到“少即是多”这一准则，羁绊、职业、角色能力、祝福、药水、装备、道具对于一个自走棋游戏来说要素实在是太多太杂了，爬塔能成功是因为对游戏影响最大的只有卡牌、遗物、药水，没有杂糅太多东西，让玩家能够专注于对这三者的策略思考和选择。 三也是最重要的一点，我说的难听一些，[b] 制作组根本不懂自走棋 [/b] 自走棋类游戏的好玩之处在哪？首先我们要从一个看起来毫不相关的东西说起——麻将。 麻将最好玩的地方是什么，三个字——胡大牌！不管是国士无双还是四暗刻，清一色还是大四喜，凑成大牌然后爽吃分是每个麻将人的梦想。相同的三张就是升星，距胜利更进一步，凑羁绊就是做能胡牌的牌型/役，最后还需要一个锦上添花的雀头来满足相应的牌型。 自走棋最大的策略性就在于羁绊和职业的组合、提升，这方面做明白了，其他元素都是次要的。而这游戏6人口封顶的设定就大大降低了游戏的爽感和策略性，你能想象麻将只需要6张牌就能胡牌吗，那我无脑拿三张一样的（升星）不一样也是赢，没有多人口羁绊就意味着没办法做大牌，胡断幺九和胡十三幺能是一个爽感吗？

从物品,局外成长,棋子数量,羁绊特点,无一不透露着制作组的保守。然而一个单机游戏不需要这样。目前感觉毫无爽点,甚至去玩云顶都比这个好玩。 或许游戏内容已经足够了,但是能得到的体验完全不值这个价格。建议还是降低一下平衡性,多给点极端的数值,以及装备的效果和自由度。 至于诅咒,个人感觉是个还算成功的设计。诅咒其实是一种资源,前期基本完全没有影响,但是拿到8个左右就比较难受了,经常一场战斗打完回1血,拿牌反而要掉2血,因此你需要规划好哪些资源值得耗费一个诅咒。不拿诅咒基本死路一条。

作为一个魔兽、炉石、云顶之奕的老自走棋玩家，我一直都希望自走棋这种有趣的玩法能像战棋一样拥有自己的游戏体系，而非局限在PVP中，所以这款单机PVE自走棋刚发售就让我眼前一亮。可惜的是《传说与战术自走棋》没有太多RPG和冒险元素，只是个单纯的爬塔游戏，据说是《杀戮尖塔》某团队的作品，确实有些《杀戮尖塔》味的，但游戏内容和质量目前还差强人意，大家需要理性购买。 [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38287879]网易UU鉴赏家培养计划[/url][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 极速畅玩，联机日友，加速社区，记得来UU哦_(:з」∠)_ [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] [h1]新颖的框架，空洞的内里 [/h1] 市面上难得的单机自走棋，光这一点就能吸引住很多玩家的目光，框架和方向十分新颖，可惜游戏内里并没有填充起来，如今比较空洞单薄，空洞在方方面面。 既然是作为一款桌面游戏，那么完全可以将桌面打造得精致有趣些，现在桌面还只是一张贴图，棋子角色毫无配音，也不存在自己的出场将效，所有的棋子打得千篇一律，打得默默无闻，丝毫没有记忆点，哪怕已经玩了好几天，我也记不住任何一个棋子的名称、样貌、羁绊。这点可以学习一下隔壁《炉石传说》如何将卡牌角色塑建得饱满立体，哪怕对于国服玩家来说炉石已经不复存在了，我也永远会记得那只小小的“塔斯丁狗”，而《传说与战术自走棋》离这种充实饱满还有很长一段路要走。 [u] 它现在就像一个具有特色的房屋框架，你走进去拍拍立柱，看看大梁，感慨这样的房屋设计以后建起来一定住得不错。那现在怎么样？你看着只有地基和框架的屋子，缺墙少壁，四面漏风，笑了笑说：现在怎么住得了人呢？ [/u] [h1]重复的流程，残缺的汉化 [/h1] 这个游戏目前只是个半成品，最影响游戏体验的是它连汉化都没做好，就打着有中文的标签卖给了国区的玩家，实际上游戏里的中文残缺不全，全程需要顶着一片中文一片英文的迷茫半玩半猜。游戏剧情有英有中就算了，人物介绍蹦段英文也没事，可是装备效果和棋子羁绊都有不少没汉化，仅有的那些汉化还是梆梆硬的机翻，狗屁不通，哭笑不得，属实有点让人难玩。 抛开汉化不谈，游戏内容也并不完善，现在只有短短的一套流程量复玩，重复的开头，重复的过场，重复的说辞，重复的剧情，敷衍了事地让人玩上一把又一把，每把除了自己玩的阵容不同之外几乎什么都一样，这样下来很容易就审美疲劳了。 [h1]单调的玩法，局限的搭配 [/h1] 《传说与战术自走棋》的内核当然是自走棋玩法，但阵容最多是六人口，棋子最历害是三费卡，上限也有点太低了，相当于《杀戮尖塔》固定五张卡牌就成形，麻将设定自摸一次就胡牌的感觉，体会不到挑战性，无脑找同一羁绊的棋子上场就能赢，上限六人口，搭配不出太多花样，对于肉鸽游戏来说缺少随机性和多样性实在是有些致命了。 [h1]满文大肆批判，反手还是好评 [/h1] 作为一个抢先体验游戏，如今的不完善、不完整、不完美也是情理之中，这段时间每天打开Steam都能发现它又有新的更新内容，可见制作方也正在用心地日益打磨它，今天存在的问题可能明天就会被加以改进，态度令人欣慰。 我愿意支持这个题材、这支队伍、这份创意，希望他们以后终能把一份优质的单机自走棋游戏端到玩家面前，但如果正式版还是现在的质量的话，我想我会把这条评价改成差评的。

2023.08.18评测 目前版本能玩，但是还不够好，满足了我需求一个“可以随时启动对局的单机”、“有重复游玩价值”、“画面不拉跨”、“自走棋”等要素的要求。对于roguelike玩法而言，确实有一定的可重复度，但是，还存在一些缺点 1、汉化不完全，部分词条存在汉化错误或者未汉化 2、对局交互不明显，虽然自己一直在洗牌摸牌，但是对于敌人而言，自己阵容缺少针对性或者被针对性 3、部分阵营是真的强，异形5级8蓝上限，一局轻松上万输出

To me, this game is worth $25 (and it's currently on sale for half that price)...(and even when it's not on sale it's only $18). I've read a few reviews (of various games) where people mention the apparent "love" or "passion" a developer has for their product, especially with respect to reviews written for Early Access games. I can't remember when I bought T&T, maybe 2022? I played it every now and then, not really following the evolution of the game. But... My latest play-through showed me just how far this game has come. I'll spare you the details, and instead just ask you to look over the games numerous patch notes to see what "love" and "passion" for a product look like. My effusiveness aside, let explain (with bullet-points) why I like this game: - You can play with one hand - It's deep, but not complicated - Combat and itemization feels impactful...like...that dinosaur really did just shoot an icicle...and now it's shooting the icicle more often because I gave it more mana regen. - Damage numbers can be seen, and they are accurate - The damage charts are fun to look at after the battle - Really great balance between tanking, healing, and DPS compositions: some runs I made a very defensive or long-lasting team, and other runs I made a team where I just blitz the enemy team with damage. And both were fun to strategize over and tweak depending on the enemy comp, "scenario effects" (like tornadoes), and available items. - I applaud Table 9 for mitigating that awful %^$#@#$ feeling when you just can't seem to roll that last copy of your minion to upgrade it; I stopped playing Dota Underlords when spent like 99 (whatever the max was?) gold and I didn't get a %^$#@#$ copy of the last Troll Warlord I needed to make him 3-star. I've never felt that way in any play-through of T&T, and I've done dozens. - So much for bullet points Great game and great job Table 9! (And great price) (And you know I had to end this review with a sentence in parenthesis) (I like to interject) (Probably because I'm bipolar) (And someone is going to think I'm Bipolar with one hand, lol).

如果你是冲着自走棋来的，那么不推荐，很不推荐 一、这玩意说白了还是地下城自己组小队那一套，羁绊的作用有，但是和没有也没什么区别，每种羁绊只有两层，而且特点也不鲜明，定位十分模糊。 二、角色卡的设计也有问题，每个种族只有五六张卡，自由度及其低下。 三、人口上限绝大多数时候只有6人口，你想要的自走棋完全不存在（我说实话6人口的自走棋游戏就是纯纯的垃圾）。 四、更新慢的一比，一年过去了也没见更几个棋子，你要是不会做就别惦记你那b原创了，搞点传统意义上的法师战士都算好的。 总结一下就是冲着自走棋来的你就别买，不是冲着自走棋来的（说实话除了自走棋我都不知道这玩意有啥卖点）可以试试。

只有六个格子的自走棋。。。根本凑不出来几个羁绊，一般也就凑3种。如果要把主种族羁绊（龙、兽人、恶魔等）达到2级（一般要4或5个同种族单位），那么副羁绊（射手、斗士、萨满等）也就最多凑1个了。 这种情况下我感觉刷新就很无聊，经常刷新池子后啥也买不到，因为可选的很少，在队伍成型后也不会再轻易调整队伍结构了，因为三连可以最多4次（三连后的角色可以再和一个三连的同角色升阶，最多四阶），手牌里囤积的也就是已经有的单位了。而且不同阵营和不同单位打起来的感觉没有特别有差异化，玩几局说实话就无聊了。

[b]I enjoyed the campaign structure, player choice, risk/reward chaos dungeons, gameplay speed settings & overall theme of Tales & Tactics but the experience suffers upon launch with elements that a new player or someone coming from a continuously supported & refined product might find archaic, overwhelming or frustrating .[/b] Quick examples: The screen is always loud with colour & imagery, the UI is information overload with a surplus of text & graphics, units lack distinct visual identity in shops & on the board, the combat visuals are homogenized despite trait differences, the shop odds are frustrating for specific traits, item removers need to be purchased, the default max unit count is 6, traits either feel great or simply suck at all levels and there's little room to synergize units with various traits. That being said T&T's UI & tabletop visuals are thematically perfect for the mechanics of the game but they are quite overwhelming when you're trying to understand what separates T&T from other auto battlers mechanically. [b]My prior experience in the genre comes from years of Teamfight Tactics & Hyper Roll. Therefor I may have a warped view on the quality & direction baseline for other auto battling projects, given that TFT has RIOT Games backing them & sees constant attention, adjustments & fixes.[/b] [i]Regardless, the following are a few critical notes & comments from my (as of writing) 12 hours playtime with added detail to the above listings.[/i] [list] [*]A majority of visuals lack distinction. Upon launching it felt terrible to acclimate myself to the game when I was overloaded with colour & swarmed with information & graphics. Even after 12 hours the screen & UI elements feel cluttered & overwhelming when it comes to components & tooltip information, despite fitting the themes of the game. [*]A lot of units look very similar to each other in their shop portraits, even more so on the board during combat. Unit's trait identifiers homogenize despite mechanical differences, most notably Orcs & Reptiles, Demons, and Dragons & Fae. [*]Upgrading units by purchasing multiple copies of them seems to be a swing in the dark for improving their effectiveness. Some units will become powerhouses while others barely change; yet due to the limited unit count allowed on your board (6) upgrading your unit’s level is the only feasible option & gameplay loop outside of items & tabletop integration. [*]The tabletop itself changing is always great because it fits with the adventure of dungeon crawling, battling through the outskirts & rising through the tournament, but the actual battles feel unsatisfying to watch with overloading or lacklustre effects & once again homogenized unit visuals. [*]Tool tips feel overly large for the information and a lot of information is presented at once despite tool tips hiding deeper explanation. [*]An unlocks screen exists to "hide" a considerable amount of content & information from a new players eyes which is great given the abundance of information presented upon loading but even with the reduced appearance there's a lot to learn. [*]The "hidden" unlockable content can be enabled by earning points through gameplay feats or you can reveal them outright if you want everything upon launch. The choice to hide mechanics & extra traits was a great choice as without it I think I may have dropped the game due to information overload. I really enjoyed the unlocked components, traits & story elements but a few of them seem too reliant on RNG for use. [*]The traits interface only displays a set amount of traits rather than the full list available on your board & while you're essentially limited to one trait per playthrough, if you can acquire enough banners (trait emblems) the list extends beyond visibility. [*]The Risk Reward elements are great, since it initiates on player choice & action. The dungeon encounters have items & debuff’s thematic to their story & how you interact. The debuff’s you can gain from the dungeons affect your board strength or assist in you in some form so the narrative isn't just fluff. D20 Dice rolls for loot at the cost of gaining chaos (a passive resource that locks you from shop purchases unless you pay health) is always thrilling to roll and the various merchants that offer items & ways to counteract chaos are a sight for sore eyes when you just don't hit big.[/list] [h3]Current Conclusion [/h3] I would cautiously recommend Tales & Tactics to those who are looking for something other than the mainstays in the genre but I would only recommend picking it up during sales when it drops to around $5AUD. There's a lot of information in Tales & Tactics but also a lot of fun & progression.

Very solid rogue auto battler. Very enjoyable game loop which gives you a lot of control over its RNG rogue aspects. I played all the way through its entire ascension and dipped into the "multiplayer" (Semi multiplayer, its not live runs, but you do face off against other peoples real builds.) While I do recommend the game it does have a couple cons: While I hate RNG and prefer control, this game gives you perhaps to much control. You pretty much decide 90% of your build at the start of every run, and the only RNG is whether you get some over powered buffs / events / items as you go. It is a weird thing for me to complain about, as this SHOULD be a pro, but it feels like it has gone to far in the controlled direction. There seems to be a very small handful of very powerful tribes, and many very weak ones. Perhaps I am missing something, and just played the other options wrong, but the power gap between good tribes and bad tribes felt pretty wide. In general the mechanical clarity of your options feels a bit lacking. Its hard to get a good measure of the smaller points and numbers of the game and you just sort of have to go off a general vibe of how successful you are, which is part of why I am not sure if I was missing something about many of the tribes or if the balance is just in question. And last: I see that the game has "seasonal multiplayer" and I have almost no idea what that means, how rank works, or much of anything along those lines. If there was a bit more clarity on what is going on in multiplayer, and perhaps a bit of better balance this game could have hooked me for a long time. - So TLDR: Definitely recommend the game, playing through the story mode is fun and really scratches that auto battler itch. As for long term multi player / replayability it is lacking a little, so a good 20-100 hour game, but its not one that is likely to hook you for hundreds.

It's a roguelike autobattler (the player chooses the fighters for their team, and then the fight happens automatically). At the beginning, you choose a character from nine available, each with different abilities. Then, over the course of the run, you build your team. The fighters on your team can be selected from randomly drawn pools, and if three more copies of the same fighter are found, they are upgraded to level four. Between fights, random events occur, which generally offer advantages (equipment, potions, special abilities, etc.). This is my first time playing this type of game (I like turn-based combat games that allow you to have complete control of the fight), and I have to say I had a lot of fun. I particularly appreciated: The enormous variety of fighters, allowing for countless different combinations and strategies. The draft option, which allows you to combine the characteristics of the starting characters to create alternative builds. The downsides are: Dependence on luck in drawing the necessary fighters: upgrading fighters is essential to progressing in the game, but if you're unlucky, you won't find the copies you need and will be defeated. Since there are so many fighters, it's common to miss the copies you need. This weakness is mitigated by items that make the search easier. This problem is particularly noticeable at high levels. Difficulty in determining party strength: during combat, fighters move independently and sometimes adopt strategies you hadn't anticipated. E’ un gioco roguelike autobattler (il giocatore sceglie i combattenti che faranno parte della sua squadra e poi il combattimento avviene in automatico). All’inizio si sceglie un personaggio tra i nove a disposizione ognuno con abilità differenti. Poi nel corso della run si forma la propria squadra. I combattenti della squadra si possono selezionare da pool pescate casualmente e se si trovano altre tre copie dello stesso combattente avviene l’upgrade fino al quarto livello. Tra un combattimento e l’altro ci sono eventi casuali che generalmente offrono dei vantaggi (equipaggiamento, pozioni, abilità particolari ecc). E’ la prima volta che provo questa tipologia di gioco ( a me piacciono i giochi con il combattimento a turni in modo da aver il completo controllo dello scontro) e devo dire che mi sono divertito molto. In particolare ho apprezzato: l’enorme varietà di combattenti che permettono di ottenere tantissime combinazioni e strategie differenti. L’opzione draft che permette di combinare le caratteristiche dei personaggi iniziali creando build alternative. I punti negativi sono: dipendenza dalla fortuna nel pescare i combattenti necessari: fare l’upgrade dei combattenti è fondamentale per avanzare nel gioco ma se le pescate sono sfortunate, non trovi le copie che ti servono e vieni sconfitto. Dato che i combattenti sono molti, avviene frequentemente di non trovare le copie che servono. Questa debolezza è mitigata da alcuno oggetti che facilitano la ricerca. Il problema si avverte in maniera rilevante agli alti livelli. Difficoltà nel capire la forza del party: durante lo scontro i combattenti si muovono in autonomia e a volte adottano strategie che non avevi previsto.

Play Time: 79.9 hours Achievements: 68 of 68. 100% Date/Version: July 17th 2026 / 1.4.34 Rating: 9 out of 10 Tales & Tactics is an Auto Battler , Hex Grid, Rouge-lite, tactics game. In this game you'll begin by selecting a difficulty, selecting a “champion”, and essentially starting your run. Within each run you'll recruit members of your team. Your team needs to synchronize with each unit, and honestly you may have to shift strategies at some points. Your team will consist of upwards 6 to 8 units by the end of the game run. Each unique “tribe” has their own trait, these traits will either offer benefits to that “tribe” of units or the tribe plus other units. There is a very small story element and an announcer whom you can disable. You'll go on an “adventure” where you select 1 of the two actions after each encounter. Random events will pop up offering tempting prices or some prices with some consequences. You'll obtain passives like “artifacts/perks” in the game that'll help your run and rarely hurt your run. In addition there are a nice chunk of items you can equip to your units, help your main character with the run, and items you can equip can be combined to create powerful combinations. Note that there is meta progression in this game, this meta progression is used to unlock content. You can beat the game without unlocking these as this content just adds more variety but also allows for runs to be not super RNG heavy. I found the difficulty to be manageable until you reach the way higher difficulties where it's just a bit too much work. I believe the runs themselves are probably 45 minutes long if not longer but I wasn't really keeping track. (Potential Spoilers) Units: You have 111 unique units you may at one point recruit for your team and/or face off against. Each unit has something unique to them ranging from their stats, abilities, and appearance. Granted their appearances hex board don't fully reflect their model portrait... just a personal thought. Each unit belongs to a particular tribe/faction/trait. Some units have 3 different traits and some may have 1 or 2 pending on your perks you have on your main character. These units you'll have a bench they can be placed in, and an active battle hexboard. Duplicates of a unit can combine to increase the units level. Level 4 is the default max of each unit, but your units can go to level 5 via special things. You have to roll for units to see what random units come up for you to purchase. Tribes/Factions/Traits: There are 37 unique traits in this game. As I mentioned before each unit has 1 to 3 unit traits. Think of these traits as “tribes/factions” in my own words. For instance if you have 3 trickster traits active you'll obtain a very unique trickster item you can equip to your units. Another example is the “Pack” trait where if you have 3 units with the pack trait you get +1 to your Army Size, and if you have 6 units with the pack traits you get +2 to your army size (team size). Like any game some of these passives may not be equally as strong, may not work as well against other teams, and may be better early, mid, or late game. This was a fun aspect to learn, and the game “allows” you to shift your teams meta if you notice the opportunities. Items you can Equip: You'll have 8 base items that can be utilize to combine into each other to make up a total of 38 unique combinations (I think) my math may be wrong. But it doesn't stop there, we have an additional 123 event style items that your units will be able to equip. Just like with any game some of these even items may have some negative consequences with them. Some will even change your units ability. It's honestly a fun concept and allows for some unique team combinations. In addition we have Banners you can equip, these banners will provide your unit with another units “trait/tribe/faction”, and will offer additional benefits such as +24 attack speed. Consumables: Consumables are items your character can use. You got 15 basic consumables and 64 special consumables. Consumables can do a variety of things such as increase a units attack speed, disable an opponent for a few seconds, even providing you with a unit you haven't obtained yet on your run. Consumables can help you reduce your curse level which becomes a huge factor as you increase your difficulty. Curse: Once you increase your game difficulty you'll start with curses, each curse gives a 5% chance of a rolled unit. Honestly sometimes you just have to embrace the curse. When a unit is cursed they are chained. Unchaining them costs you 1 life point. You typically start with 6 life points, 2 being 1 time passive live points. You can gain more life points by winning battles. End Game Currency: It's used to unlock for events, items, units, traits, etc... You can beat the game without using unlocks and this game does a great job by not making your runs impossible because you've added so much additional content. Yes there are elements of RNG but they don't destroy the game. And unlike several games I've played where when you unlock more content it just adds too much randomness and makes the game just.. well random this game doesn't do that in my opinion. Achievements: Mass majority of these achievements are not RNG heavy what so ever. Yes there are a very few but almost every run I was able to achieve at least 1 achievement, and it's possible to get 2 or 3 achievements per run. The developers want you to play the game is all. Unlike some games where the achievements are 1% event that happens maybe 1 time in 100 runs. Final Thoughts: This is a MUST BUY! For any person who loves the auto-battler, team building games. I super enjoyed myself and look forward to additional content that I'm assuming is going to come. Another recommendation I have is The Last Flame if you haven't already played that game. PROS: Unique Tribes/Factions/Traits Unique Units Nice Learning curve Unique Items Unique Consumables Game Play Length of runs Short but simple story Speed and pause settings Save mechanics NEUTRAL: Art – Portraits don't align with some of the unit models CONS:
